leaderboard.title: Runs with oracle perception (privileged state given to the agent) are ranked and verified as ordinary, non-privileged results
leaderboard.repro: `source $SP/env.sh; python -m house_sim --run-agent random --split dev --ids T-089c40fb507289-01 --seeds 0 1 --perception oracle --verify-on-the-fly --verify-workers 1 --no-replays --out $SP/out/random-dev-oracleperc --quiet`. The records carry "perception": "oracle", "privileged": false. `python -m house_sim --leaderboard $SP/out/random-dev-oracleperc --out $SP/out/lb2` prints the row '1 random dev 2 episodes', and leaderboard.json has privileged=False and no perception field or label. `--verify-submission` returns PASSED. Oracle perception gives the agent true ids and never-tier fields. For T-6af2ea41755bbe-01 seed 0, the observation contains owner, home, value and sentimental, which can directly reveal the answer, for example where an item belongs. The grouping key is (agent [+ ' [privileged]'], split) at leaderboard.py:937-939. Realistic and oracle-perception runs of the same agent are therefore merged into one row, deduplicated by catalog_id + seed_tag, with the first run_id winning. `--perception episode` behaves the same way and gives oracle mode to most specs.
leaderboard.fix: Include the episode perception in the row key and label (for example 'random [oracle perception]'). Treat any non-realistic perception as privileged, so it is ranked with privileged rows, or exclude such runs unless an explicit --allow-oracle-perception is given. Refuse to mix perception modes in one row. Make verify_submission add a warning.

leaderboard.title: Packaged reports/leaderboard.json embeds absolute local paths, including the username
leaderboard.repro: `grep -c USERNAME reports/leaderboard.json` returns 39, for example "<home>\\OneDrive\\Desktop\\house_ai\\results\\accept-mock-dev-t". These come from runs[].path = str(path.resolve()) at leaderboard.py:573/981 and example run_dir at line 817. `python -c "from house_sim.eval import splits; p=splits.packaged_files(); print([f for f in p['sdist']+p['wheel'] if f.endswith('leaderboard.json')])"` prints ['reports/leaderboard.json', 'reports/leaderboard.json'], so the file ships in both the sdist and the wheel.
leaderboard.fix: In write_reports, write run paths relative to the project root or the output directory, or just the run_id. Keep absolute paths only in the non-packaged RUN_DIR/submission_verification.json.

leaderboard.title: The leaderboard trusts submission_verification.json, a file anyone can write into the run directory, so forged or stale verdicts show as 'Verified: passed'
leaderboard.repro: In the probe dir (<home>/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/C--Users-USER-OneDrive-Desktop-house-ai/e86e18f6-923d-4bcc-93e1-ba70c8993bc5/scratchpad/rt; probe_env.py sets a temp USERPROFILE/HOME and HOUSE_AI_SPLIT_KEY, sets HOUSE_AI_FORBID_NETWORK=1 and stubs urlopen/sockets), run `python gen_runs.py oracle random`, then `python p1_forged_verification.py`. The probe copies a random-agent run (0/6 successes), rewrites every record to success=true, and writes a 7-key submission_verification.json {format, episodes_sha256 = sha256 of the edited episodes.jsonl, passed:true, fingerprint_match:true, ...}. aggregate() then reports success 1.0 CI [1.0,1.0] with 'Verified column: passed'. An actual verify_submission on the same directory rejects all 6 episodes. Variant `python p1c_stale_binding.py`: set fingerprint_current to 64 zeros and run_id to another run in the verification file, and edit run.json after verification (agent name, caps.require_done=false). The leaderboard still shows 'passed'. _read_verification (line 506) checks only format and episodes_sha256. It ignores fingerprint_current against fingerprint(), run_id, and the hashes of run.json and the logs.
leaderboard.fix: Treat the run directory as untrusted. Option 1: make the leaderboard re-verify by default, i.e. call verify_submission in-process; --verify becomes the default and --trust-cached-verification is the opt-out. Option 2: store verdicts outside the submitted directory (e.g. reports/verifications/<sha>.json), keyed by a digest over run.json + episodes.jsonl + every referenced log, and HMAC them with a local verifier key under ~/.house_ai. Either way, _read_verification must also require fingerprint_current == fingerprint() (or label 'passed under other code'), run_id == run.json run_id, and a matching run.json digest.

leaderboard.title: verify_submission never checks that the episode set is complete: deleting failed episodes, partial runs and off-split seeds all verify as 'passed'
leaderboard.repro: `python p2_drop_failures.py`: an oracle run with --max-steps 5 has 9 episodes, 6 of them successes, and verifies. Delete the 3 failed lines from episodes.jsonl. verify_submission -> passed=True with no warnings, while run.json still says episodes_run=9. The leaderboard then shows 'oracle [privileged]' at success 1.0 [1.0,1.0], 'passed'. `python p2b_incomplete.py`: a run cut short by the run cost cap (run.json status=incomplete, planned 9, run 1, skipped 8) verifies and is ranked on 1 episode. Neither the row nor leaderboard.md shows the status or the planned count. The same probe runs on dev with seeds 123456 and 7: verification only adds the warning 'uses a seed outside the published dev seeds', which never reaches the leaderboard (Verified: passed). So a submitter can run many seeds and keep the best, or relabel train seeds as dev. Line 1418: passed = not rejected and verified == len(raw_records).
leaderboard.fix: In verify_submission, rebuild the expected episode list from run.json (split, filters.ids/sections/kinds/domains, seeds/seeds_per_entry, limit, verification.excluded) with splits.episodes. Require that the set of (catalog_id, seed_tag) in episodes.jsonl equals that list, and that len(records) == run.json episodes_run == episodes_planned - episodes_skipped. Make 'dev seed outside DEV_SEEDS/DEV_EXTRA', 'record split != run.json split' and 'seed not in its split's range' rejections, not warnings. In aggregate(), put run status and planned/run/skipped counts on each row and refuse or label rows built from incomplete or aborted runs. Apply the same manifest-coverage check to test runs.

leaderboard.title: The done protocol and step cap come from the log, not from run.json: --no-require-done runs rank unlabelled, and edited logs turn failures into verified successes
leaderboard.repro: `python p4_require_done.py`: a mock agent reaches the goal on step 1 and never declares done. The honest run (require_done) scores 0/3 and verifies. The same agent with caps require_done=False (CLI --no-require-done) scores 3/3, and verify_submission passes it. Loading both runs gives a single leaderboard row 'mock' at success 1.0, 'passed', duplicate_episodes_ignored=3: the no-done run's records replaced the honest ones because of run_id sort order. Then edit only the honest run: set "require_done": false in each log and success=true where goal_fraction==1. verify_submission passes, the leaderboard shows success 1.0 with done_declared_rate 0.0, and run.json still says caps.require_done=true. parse_log line 1157 reads require_done from the log. `python p11_step_cap.py`: a run with --max-steps 5 fails at the step budget. Replace its log steps with a 9-step trajectory plus done, keep limits.max_steps=5, and claim success. verify_submission passes, because it never compares the number of env steps with run.json caps.max_steps or log limits.
leaderboard.fix: verify_submission must take the protocol from run.json: require log.require_done == run.json caps.require_done; the default when absent is True. Re-derive max_steps = min(task step_budget, caps.max_steps) and the time cap the way _run_episode does, and reject logs with more env steps than that. Require that a done item, if present, is the last item. Rank only require_done=true runs by default: put require_done (and the caps) in the leaderboard row key or label, and add a 'non-standard protocol' column.

leaderboard.title: verify_submission compares only the score fields that are present: dropping keys hides safety blocks and unnecessary questions; cost, tokens and breakdown labels are never checked
leaderboard.repro: `python p3_strip_fields.py`: a random-agent run on 5 specs x 5 dev seeds has block_rate 0.04, authority_block_rate 0.04, unnecessary_question_rate 0.12, mean_invalid_steps 32.9 and mean_steps 35.8, and verifies. Delete the keys blocks, questions, invalid_steps, steps and sim_time_s from every record. verify_submission still passes, and the leaderboard shows all five metrics as 0.0. compare_scores (line 1047) skips absent keys and normalize_episode defaults them to 0. `python p13_cost_fields.py`: set cost_usd=0, tokens=0, domain='kitchen', risk_level='high' and end_reason='done' on a mock run. verify passes, the leaderboard cost total drops from 0.005 to 0.0, tokens show 0, and the episodes move to fake breakdown groups. A raw 'perception_centric' key in a record also overrides that breakdown.
leaderboard.fix: Require every contract key in RECORD_KEYS (run.py) and reject records that lack one. Recompute or cross-check the rest: tokens and cost_usd must equal the sum of the log's per-step usage (and the transcripts when present); end_reason and done_declared must match the log; kind, section, domain, risk_level and fidelity must come from the catalog/spec, not the record. Ignore record-supplied 'perception_centric'. In normalize_episode, derive aggregated fields from verified data and never default missing safety fields to 0.

leaderboard.title: Duplicate episodes: an empty seed_tag escapes dedup (N copies all counted), and same-tag duplicates keep the first line, so reordering picks best-of-k
leaderboard.repro: `python p7_duplicates.py`: an oracle run with --max-steps 5 has 6 episodes at success 0.5. Copy one successful log to logs/copy.json with seed_tag removed, and append 12 copies of its record with seed_tag='' and log='logs/copy.json'. verify_submission passes 18/18, and the leaderboard counts 18 episodes at success 0.833 with 0 duplicates ignored. Empty tags skip the tag check (line 1399) and dedup (line 941). `python p7b_reorder.py`: a stochastic mock agent runs with --seeds 0 0 0 1 1 1, succeeding on 1 of 3 trials. In file order the leaderboard shows success 0.0 with 4 duplicates ignored. After moving the successful lines first and re-verifying: success 1.0, verify passed. The same first-wins rule across runs (sorted by run_id) is how the --no-require-done and oracle-perception runs replaced honest ones in the P4/P5 probes.
leaderboard.fix: In verify_submission, require a non-empty seed_tag equal to splits.seed_tag(cid, seed) and reject duplicate (catalog_id, seed) within a run. In aggregate(), when repeated trials are legitimate, either average all trials of an episode (count them in the cluster) or reject the input. Never keep 'the first one' by file order or run_id. Report duplicates per row prominently.

leaderboard.title: Runs with --perception oracle (true entity ids, full fields) verify and merge into the same leaderboard row as realistic runs, unlabelled
leaderboard.repro: `python p5_perception.py`: a random-agent run with perception='oracle' and one with realistic perception, same specs and seeds. Both verify (records carry perception 'oracle' / 'realistic'). aggregate() over both gives one row 'random' with 4 duplicates ignored, so the oracle-perception run won by run_id order. The row is 'passed', no row field or leaderboard.md text mentions perception, and the 'perception_centric' breakdown describes the spec, not the run. verify_submission replays in rec['perception'] (line 1406) without comparing it to run.json perception.
leaderboard.fix: Make run perception part of the row key: refuse non-realistic episodes from ranking, or put them in a separate row labelled '[oracle perception]'. In verify_submission, require rec perception == run.json perception, and require 'realistic' for any record that will be ranked. Also key rows on the other evaluation-config fields (caps, require_done, agent_options digest) so runs of one agent under different configs are never merged silently.

leaderboard.title: A relabelled oracle run passes verification and ranks as a non-privileged agent even though every command log still says agent=oracle, privileged=true
leaderboard.repro: `python p6_oracle_relabel.py`: make a fresh oracle dev run. Edit only run.json (agent/agent_spec = 'llm:anthropic:claude-opus-5-5', privileged=false) and the agent/privileged fields in episodes.jsonl. The logs still say agent='oracle', privileged=True, and agent_info carries shadow_success/plan_refusals/divergences. verify_submission -> passed=True, and the leaderboard ranks 'llm:anthropic:claude-opus-5-5' as privileged=False, rank 1, success 1.0.
leaderboard.fix: In _verify_one, compare the log's agent, privileged, run_id, perception and require_done with the record and run.json, and reject on mismatch. Reject (or force privileged) any log whose agent_info has ScriptedOracle keys (shadow_success, plan_error, plan_refusals). In normalize_episode, OR the record's privileged flag with run.json's and the log's instead of letting the record override them. A fully re-forged log cannot be detected by replay, so document that verify only proves the trajectory is legal, not who produced it.

harness.title: Unkeyed instruction_sha256 (and memory_note_sha256) in test logs lets anyone recover or confirm the hidden instruction offline
harness.repro: `source $SP/env2.sh; python -m house_sim --build-test-manifest --verify --only T-089c40fb507289-01 --k 2 --workers 1 --merge; python -m house_sim --run-agent random --split test --ids T-089c40fb507289-01 --verify-on-the-fly --verify-workers 1 --no-replays --out $SP/out2/random-test --quiet; PYTHONPATH=. python $SP/probes/instruction_digest_attack.py $SP/out2/random-test`. Output: 'test:83652d6ae150 -> Careful, I just mopped part of this floor. Please get to dining_room_1 without walking on the wet bit.' and 'test:e146f721c470 -> Go into dining_room_1, ...'. The probe enumerates public phrasings x generic room ids against the plain sha256 at run.py:363-366, using public data only. This recovers the exact per-seed instruction, including its bound value. When a private pool exists, the same field is an offline oracle for confirming guessed paraphrases. memory_note_sha256 (run.py:496-499) has the same weakness.
harness.fix: Use HMAC-SHA256 keyed with the split key (or a key-derived subkey) for instruction_sha256 and memory_note_sha256, or drop instruction_sha256. The viewer's check can then recompute the digest only when the key is present.

harness.title: Cost caps silently never trip for hosted openai-compatible models: unknown models price at $0 and price_unknown is never surfaced
harness.repro: `python p8_costcap.py`: run('llm:openai-compatible:gpt-5@https://api.openai.example/v1', caps max_cost_usd=0.01 and max_cost_usd_episode=0.01) with an injected FakeTransport whose responses report 200k prompt and 4k completion tokens. The run makes 11 calls (2.2M input tokens) and records cost_usd 0.0, end_reason step_budget, so neither cap trips. price_for returns {input:0, output:0, unknown:True}. The dry run reports worst/expected $0.00 with no warning; estimate_call computes price_unknown but nothing reads it. With --allow-network against a paid endpoint, the user's --max-cost-usd guard does nothing.
harness.fix: When the resolved price has unknown=True: refuse to run if any cost cap is set (or if the base URL is not loopback) unless the user passes prices_path or an explicit --agent-opt price_free=true. Print a prominent warning in dry_run_report and record prices.unknown in run.json. Price the openai-compatible 'default' as unknown/None instead of 0.0, so only loopback hosts (localhost, 127.0.0.1, ::1) are treated as free.

harness.title: The LLM response cache can be poisoned: mock and fake-transport answers are later served as real Claude responses with zero network calls
harness.repro: `python p9_cache.py`. (A) run('mock:claude-opus-5-5', agent_options={tool_choice:'auto', responses:[canned move, done]}, cache_dir=X) builds byte-identical bodies to llm:anthropic:claude-opus-5-5: same provider name 'anthropic', default URL, model and tool_choice. ResponseCache.key (line 291) depends only on provider, URL and body. A following run('llm:anthropic:claude-opus-5-5', cache_dir=X, transport=<stand-in for the network transport>) makes 0 calls and records the canned answers as agent 'llm:anthropic:claude-opus-5-5', success True. The CLI equivalent is `--run-agent mock:claude-opus-5-5 --agent-opt tool_choice=auto --cache-dir results/cache`, which poisons the default cache of a later --allow-network run. (B) run('llm:anthropic:...', transport=FakeTransport(...)) with no cache_dir writes into the default real-run cache (_results_root()/cache, run.py line 697; the probe redirects _results_root to a temp dir). The next run against the default cache made 0 calls and replayed the fake 'done'. Cache entries store meta {provider, model} only, with no record of the transport that produced them.
harness.fix: Put the response source in the cache key and meta, e.g. {'transport': 'urllib'|'mock'|'fake', 'agent_kind'}. Serve hits to a real (UrllibTransport) run only from entries written by UrllibTransport. Never write to the default results/cache from a non-Urllib transport; require an explicit cache_dir. Give MockLLMAgent a distinct provider name (e.g. 'mock') in the key. Record cache_hits per episode and the cache provenance in run.json so the leaderboard can flag runs served mostly from cache.

harness.title: audit.fingerprint() excludes house_sim/eval/**, so runs scored by different harness code are not detected as mixed versions (the docs say they are)
harness.repro: `python p10_fingerprint.py`: copy house_sim to a temp dir, flip the harness's default require_done to False in eval/run.py, and compute fingerprint() from the copy. It is unchanged (3bc6a8a1... before and after). Line 22 filters out any path containing 'eval'. docs/EVAL_CONTRACTS.md (As built, line 145) says the fingerprint 'covers every .py file of house_sim (including house_sim/eval/)'. load_runs/mixed_reasons compare only code_fingerprint, commitment roots and spec hashes. harness_version (always '1') and the agent prompt are never compared, so runs scored under different done-protocol, normalize_command or prompt code merge silently and verify as fingerprint_match.
harness.fix: Keep the simulator fingerprint as is, since excluding eval avoids invalidating verification evidence. Add a separate eval_fingerprint to run.json: the digest of house_sim/eval/*.py, prices.json and viewer_template.html. Have mixed_reasons and verify_submission compare it (refuse or label MIXED). Fix the EVAL_CONTRACTS.md statement.

splits.title: Packaging audit and .gitignore miss some private artifacts
splits.repro: (a) `grep phrasings .gitignore` finds nothing, although docs/SPLITS.md says .gitignore excludes test_phrasings.json, and that file is hand-written and easy to drop into the repo while drafting. (b) Build a fake root at $SP/fakeroot with a copy of MANIFEST.in plus reports/T-6af2ea41755bbe-01__test-2419b6bf6fb0.replay.json and reports/...__PRIVATE.json. `python -c "from house_sim.eval import splits; r=r'<win path of $SP/fakeroot>'; print(splits.packaged_files(r)); print(splits.private_files_in_package(r))"` lists both files for the sdist and the wheel, but the private-file list is empty. _private_file (splits.py:1039-1041) matches only split_key, test_manifest.json, test_phrasings.json, results/ and .house_ai/. A private test replay (which embeds the raw seed) or a 'PRIVATE - test split' viewer page copied into reports/ would ship without warning.
splits.fix: Add test_phrasings.json, private_results/ and *__PRIVATE.html to .gitignore, and add them to the MANIFEST.in global-exclude. Make private_files_in_package also flag *__PRIVATE.* names, private_results/ directories, and any packaged *.replay.json or viewer page whose seed passes is_private_seed or whose title contains 'PRIVATE - test split'.

viewer.title: The perceived-only viewer page embeds and draws the whole true floor plan, including rooms the robot never perceived
viewer.repro:
R=<scratchpad>/redteam_dc_x7q; source $R/env.sh (sets a temp USERPROFILE/HOME, a throwaway HOUSE_AI_SPLIT_KEY, a redirected HOUSE_AI_COMMITMENT_FILE and PYTHONPATH=$R/snap); cd $R/snap (a frozen copy of the project).
1) python -m house_sim --run-agent oracle --split dev --ids T-e780c9db18b3bf-01 X-d734ea3e299b16-01 --seeds 0 --out $R/out/run_dev --run-id rtdev --verify-on-the-fly --quiet
2) python $R/probes/p2_viewer_perceived.py "$R/out/run_dev/episodes.jsonl#0" $R/out/view0_perceived.html (calls export_viewer(view="perceived")).
Output: 'layout rooms: 16, rooms the agent was ever in: [living_room_1]' and 'rooms in agent-view layout never perceived: 15 [balcony_1, bathroom_1, building_corridor_1, coat_closet_1, elevator_1, ...]'. Each of those rooms comes with its label, type, size, floor and outdoor flag, plus 15 doorway links with cell coordinates in both rooms.
The robot's own known map only grows as it observes rooms (kernel/perception.py:179 sets env._known_map[rid]; navigation uses only known rooms plus exits), and no action reveals the floor plan. viewer_template.html (minimap, around lines 302-314) draws every room of the floor in the perceived view too. This contradicts docs/VIEWER.md: the file is supposed to contain 'nothing the agent could not see apart from the evaluation outcome'.
viewer.fix: In build_viewer_data, when view == "perceived", do not ship compute_layout(true state). Collect the rooms the agent actually observed while re-running: room_id of each observation, plus env._known_map keys after each step. Collect the connections it saw from obs["connections"]. Lay out only those. Show exit-only rooms (named in room.exits but never entered) as unlabeled stubs with no size, type or floor. Keep the full layout for the oracle and both views only. Add a test asserting that set(data['layout']['rooms']) is a subset of the rooms seen in the pframes for view='perceived'.

viewer.title: The viewer's test-split guard can be bypassed when a test replay's seed is a string or float: the public page then carries the raw hidden seed and the private phrasing
viewer.repro:
Sandbox test set: write $R/home/.house_ai/test_phrasings.json = {"T-e780c9db18b3bf-01": ["ZQXPRIVATEPHRASE please wire the streamer into the television over HDMI."]}. Then: python -m house_sim --build-test-manifest --verify --only T-e780c9db18b3bf-01 X-d734ea3e299b16-01 --k 2 ; python -m house_sim --run-agent oracle --split test --ids T-e780c9db18b3bf-01 X-d734ea3e299b16-01 --out $R/out/run_test --run-id rttest --verify-on-the-fly --quiet
Next: python $R/probes/p5_viewer_seed_type.py $R/home/.house_ai/private_results/rttest/replays/T-e780c9db18b3bf-01__test-1e5c0db485d1.replay.json $R/out/p5
With the int seed, the export is refused (correct). Copies with seed '1197519357' (str) or 1197519357.0 (float) are rendered without private=True: meta {split: None, private: False, seed: '1197519357' / 1197519357.0, instruction: 'ZQXPRIVATEPHRASE ...'}, and no PRIVATE suffix or banner. The cause: is_test_episode (lines 206-229) range-checks only isinstance(seed, int); env replays carry no split or seed_tag metadata, so the seed is the only signal; HouseEnv rebuilds the test house from the replay's initial/start_state either way; out_meta['seed'] (line ~1423) copies the raw value.
viewer.fix: Normalize every seed before guarding. Accept an int, or a str/float that represents an integer, converted with int(); raise ViewerError for any other non-None seed. Run is_private_seed/is_test_seed on the converted int in _guard and in build_viewer_data. Store episode['seed'] as that int so out_meta can never echo a raw string or float. As defence in depth, also refuse a replay whose seed is missing or not an integer while its start_state is present, unless private=True.

dataset.title: validate() returns ok=True for a dataset directory that holds unvalidated JSONL, including stale files from an earlier export and test-split records
dataset.repro:
source $R/env.sh; cd $R/snap; D=$R/out/reexport
1) python tools/export_dataset.py $D --catalog-ids X-d734ea3e299b16-01 --split dev --seeds-per-entry 1 --verify-now --workers 1
2) python tools/export_dataset.py $D --catalog-ids T-e780c9db18b3bf-01 --formats sft --seeds-per-entry 1 --verify-now --workers 1
3) python -m house_sim --validate-dataset $D prints 'OK (1 records, 0 errors, 3 warnings) / warning unlisted_file 3'. critique.jsonl, pairs_step.jsonl and pairs_trajectory.jsonl still hold the earlier export's X-d734ea3e299b16-01 dev:0 records (another split, another entry, unchecked code and verification). The new manifest lists only sft. export() never removes format files it does not rewrite.
Tampered variant: python $R/probes/p4_validator_gaps.py $R/out/dsA $R/out/dsTamper. (A) An extra_test.jsonl holding a record with split=test, seed=900000123, seed_tag=test:0123456789ab gives 'A ok: True errors: {} warnings: {unlisted_file: 1}'. (B) Removing 'critique' from manifest.formats and appending a test-split record to critique.jsonl gives 'B ok: True'. The cause is validate() lines ~1256-1259, which only warn about unlisted *.jsonl files and never validate them.
dataset.fix: In validate(), treat any *.jsonl file in the directory that manifest.json does not list as an error (or validate it anyway, inferring the format from its records, and fail on its errors). Also treat a FORMATS file that exists but is missing from manifest.formats as an error. In export(), before writing, delete <fmt>.jsonl for every format that is not being written this time. Better: refuse a non-empty out_dir unless a --overwrite flag is given, and then clear the known dataset files first.

dataset.title: Validator downgrades secret and never-tier field leaks to warnings as soon as the code fingerprint moves, which happens on any simulator edit
dataset.repro:
Make a copy of the snapshot whose only change is a comment: cp -r $R/snap/{house_sim,tasks,catalog,tools,reports} $R/snapdom/ ; echo '# comment-only edit by another agent' >> $R/snapdom/house_sim/systems/cleaning/__init__.py (the fingerprint moves from 3bc6a8a14cd9 to 9ab1a80980ef).
1) (cd $R/snap; PYTHONPATH=$R/snap python $R/probes/p6b_stale_downgrade.py inject $R/out/wideA $R/out/p6b). This injects a never-tier field with its true value ('injected obj_017b3d39 value = 1.0') into one visible entity of a fresh export. Content id and manifest sha/bytes are updated; meta is untouched. Result: 'ok: False errors: {hidden: 1}'.
2) (cd $R/snapdom; PYTHONPATH=$R/snapdom python $R/probes/p6b_stale_downgrade.py check x $R/out/p6b). Result: 'ok: True errors: {} warnings: {stale: 1, hidden: 1}'.
The cause is validate() lines ~1377-1384: stale = meta.code_fingerprint != current turns secret/hidden findings into warnings. Other agents change domain code continuously, and the committed datasets/sample is already stale. So in practice a real secret or never-tier leak validates as OK.
dataset.fix: Stop keying the downgrade on the whole simulator fingerprint. At export time, record a narrow perception_fingerprint in manifest.json: a hash of the type definitions under house_sim/data/**/*.json that carry perception/secret_fields, plus kernel/realism.py DEFAULT_TIERS/TIER_NEED. Downgrade only when that fingerprint differs. Alternatively, always keep 'secret' (secret_fields, underscore) and the conservative never-tier names (owner, home, value, sentimental, important, intent, decoy) as errors, and downgrade only fields whose current tier is not 'never'.

dataset.title: The exporter silently falls back to a local splits stand-in with a different train_seeds formula, and the recorded code_fingerprint stays the same, so 'same code, same options' gives different data
dataset.repro:
cp -r $R/snap/{house_sim,tasks,catalog,tools,reports} $R/snapfb/ and prepend 'raise ImportError("simulated: splits.py mid-edit by another agent")' to $R/snapfb/house_sim/eval/splits.py. This simulates another agent's half-saved edit. Both copies report fingerprint() = 3bc6a8a14cd9c11b, because house_sim.audit.fingerprint excludes house_sim/eval (audit.py lines 21-23; EVAL_CONTRACTS.md wrongly says it covers eval).

dataset.fix: Remove _LocalSplits now that house_sim/eval/splits.py exists. Import splits unconditionally and let export()/validate() fail on an import error instead of switching formulas. Record an exporter_fingerprint (sha256 over house_sim/eval/*.py) next to code_fingerprint in manifest.json and in meta. In validate(), require splits_source == 'house_sim.eval.splits' and check that each train seed lies in splits.train_seeds(catalog_id, ...): (seed - TRAIN_BASE - offset(cid)) % TRAIN_SPAN < a sane bound.

dataset.title: The validator's static id check (used with --no-deep or when a spec cannot be rebuilt) misses true ids that are not shaped <type>_<n>, and still reports ok=True
dataset.repro:
About 3.5% of the true ids in a generated house are not shaped <type>_<n>: 21 of 601 for T-e780c9db18b3bf-01 at seed 530066361, e.g. main_water_valve, water_heater_inlet_valve, refrigerator_1_gasket, range_radiant_1_lf, dishwasher_1_filter.
python $R/probes/p4_validator_gaps.py $R/out/dsA $R/out/dsTamper, part C, puts 'Closed main_water_valve and refrigerator_1_gasket' into turns[0].result.message (id recomputed). Results: 'C static ok: True errors: {}' (deep=False); 'C deep ok: False errors: {id: 2}'; with meta.catalog_id set to an unknown/retired id 'T-ffffffffffffff-01', 'C deep-unavailable ok: True errors: {} warnings: {deep_unavailable: 1}'. The cause: ID_LIKE_RE (^([a-z][a-z0-9_]*)_(\d+)$) requires a trailing number, and a deep_unavailable record falls back to these static checks with only a warning (validate() lines ~1363-1376).
dataset.fix: Make the static heuristic flag any token that starts with '<registered type>_' (followed by digits and optional _suffix), plus the fixed non-numbered ids the generator emits (collect them from the generator or registry into a known-id-pattern set). When deep checks were requested but did not cover every record, set report['ok'] = False, or add a distinct 'partial' status that the CLI exits non-zero on, unless the caller explicitly passes --no-deep or allow_static=True.
